story.title: Swedes Vote in Pivotal Election That May Bring Far-Right Party into Government
story.summary: Voting is underway in Sweden's general election, which could see the far-right Sweden Democrats enter government for the first time. The election follows a closely contested campaign marked by intense political polarization, with the ruling right-wing bloc and the center-left opposition in a tight race. Key issues influencing voters include immigration and crime, reflecting a significant shift in Sweden's political landscape.

explore_lenses.label: Why would Sweden Democrat cabinet seats matter?
explore_lenses.title: From outside support to direct power
explore_lenses.summary: The Sweden Democrats have supported the incumbent right-wing government from outside the cabinet; entering government would give them formal ministerial responsibility rather than only parliamentary leverage. That outcome is contingent on the right-wing bloc retaining enough support to form a government.

claims.text: Since 2022, Ulf Kristersson has led a three-party centre-right coalition that depends on the Sweden Democrats for a parliamentary majority, while the party has remained outside the cabinet.

Kristersson said in April that the Moderates would allow the Sweden Democrats into government if the right-wing bloc wins a majority, while maintaining that he would remain prime minister even if the Sweden Democrats won more votes than his party.
Whether the party receives ministries, and which ones, remains unresolved on election day because it depends on the final parliamentary balance and post-election government negotiations.

explore_lenses.label: What are Kristersson and Andersson offering?
explore_lenses.title: Crime and migration versus welfare and cooperation
explore_lenses.summary: The leading blocs are presenting different priorities, although both are competing in an election shaped heavily by migration and public safety. Their public arguments also differ over whether Sweden Democrat influence would be an acceptable basis for government.

claims.text: Kristersson has said his government’s focus is improving everyday life after its crackdown on organised crime and immigration.
Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson has pledged stronger welfare provision and assistance for households facing higher living costs.
Andersson argues that a government dominated by the Sweden Democrats would be unprecedented and instead calls for a government led by her in a “new spirit of cooperation.”
Associated Press reported that the campaign has been fragmented, with questions about viable governing combinations overshadowing some policy debates, including health-care organization.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the votes are counted?
explore_lenses.title: Recount, Speaker talks, then a confidence vote
explore_lenses.summary: Swedes elect the Riksdag, not a prime minister directly. The official result and the parties’ ability to avoid a parliamentary majority against a proposed prime minister determine who can govern.

claims.text: The Riksdag says the result remains preliminary while votes are recounted, a process that takes about a week; the incumbent prime minister may nevertheless announce in the following days whether he intends to stay or resign.

The newly elected Riksdag is scheduled to convene on September 28, 2026, when it elects a Speaker; the Speaker plays the central role in proposing a prime minister after consultations with party leaders.

A proposed prime minister is approved unless more than half of the Riksdag’s members vote against the proposal; if four Speaker proposals fail, an extraordinary election must be held within three months.

story_report.summary: Swedes are voting in a closely contested, polarized general election that could bring the far-right Sweden Democrats into government for the first time. The immediate outcome will shape whether Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing bloc can retain power and begin negotiations on a new cabinet, or whether the centre-left opposition can form an alternative government. Immigration, crime, welfare and household living costs have featured in a campaign also shaped by uncertainty over which governing combinations are viable.

sections.heading: Sweden Democrats’ Role in Government
sections.body: Kristersson has led a three-party centre-right coalition since 2022 that relies on the Sweden Democrats for a parliamentary majority, although the party has remained outside the cabinet. In April, he said the Moderates would permit the Sweden Democrats to enter government if the right-wing bloc won a majority. He also said he would remain prime minister even if the Sweden Democrats received more votes than his party.

sections.heading: Competing Campaign Priorities
sections.body: Kristersson has said his government is focused on improving everyday life after its crackdown on organised crime and immigration. Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson has promised stronger welfare services and support for households facing higher living costs. She has argued that a Sweden Democrat-dominated government would be unprecedented and called instead for a government led by her in a “new spirit of cooperation.”

sections.heading: Riksdag Government Formation Process
sections.body: The result remains preliminary while votes are recounted, a process the Riksdag says takes about a week, although the incumbent prime minister may announce in the following days whether he intends to remain or resign. The newly elected Riksdag is due to convene on September 28, when it elects a Speaker who consults party leaders and proposes a prime minister. A nominee takes office unless more than half of lawmakers vote against the proposal.

unresolved.text: A right-bloc victory would not by itself determine whether the Sweden Democrats receive ministerial posts, which portfolios they might hold, or the final cabinet composition; those questions depend on the parliamentary balance and post-election negotiations.
The timing and outcome of the first vote on a prime minister, which could occur no earlier than September 29, depend on the final result and coalition talks.
Election-day reporting does not establish which campaign priorities will prevail in coalition negotiations or in the next government’s final program.

related_stories.summary: Wisconsin Congressman Tom Tiffany sustained minor injuries after his plane made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday. Tiffany, who is also a candidate for governor, was returning from a Republican fundraising dinner when the aircraft lost power. He reportedly had to swim to safety following the incident.

related_stories.title: Iran Reports Casualty in US Attack on Commercial Ship in Hormuz
related_stories.summary: Iranian authorities have reported that one crew member was killed when an Iranian commercial ship was struck near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The Qeshm governor attributed the attack to a 'terrorist enemy,' though the exact nature of the projectile remains unidentified. This incident marks a continuation of tensions between the US and Iran in the region.
